::: {.workshop-kicker}
Supplied route · synthetic continuous trace · not a live system record
:::

This synthetic dialogue is structured to resemble the current Socratic Oracle interaction: the Oracle first displays a paper-grounded challenge, the researcher answers aloud or by keyboard, a voice response is reviewed as text before it is sent, and the next displayed turn stays with the active issue. The dialogue, state progression, and coding were written for the workshop. They are **not** output from a real session and are not evidence about how reliably the live service behaves.

In the deployed interface, “voice” describes the researcher's input. The Oracle's questions remain on screen; the site does not read them aloud.

Read the [fictional sample case](sample-case.html) first if you need the proposal context.

::: {.code-key}
<span><i class="code-c">C</i> confirmed</span>
<span><i class="code-r">R</i> reframed</span>
<span><i class="code-x">X</i> challenged</span>
<span><i class="code-m">M</i> misread</span>
<span><i class="code-star">★</i> meaningful</span>
:::

## One possible coding

Codes describe the movement of the exchange, not the quality of the researcher or proposal. More than one coding may be defensible.

| Moment | Code | Evidence | Why this reading is plausible |
|---|:---:|---|---|
| Turns 1–3 | <i class="code-x">X</i> <i class="code-star">★</i> | The opening cites the absent comparison, and the follow-up asks what survives without causal attribution. | The sequence presses the consequence of a limitation rather than simply naming it. |
| Turn 4 | <i class="code-r">R</i> | “Reported change within this cohort” replaces a causal effect claim. | The topic remains, but the evidential boundary changes. |
| Turns 5–6 | <i class="code-m">M</i> | The Oracle introduces critique quality even though the proposal measures confidence. | The researcher identifies and corrects a construct substitution. |
| Turns 7–8 | <i class="code-r">R</i> <i class="code-star">★</i> | Participation counts become descriptive rather than evidence of confidence or quality. | The correction is followed rather than ignored, and the role of one evidence source is bounded. |
| Turn 9 | <i class="code-c">C</i> | The closure recaps the student-owned limits without asking another question. | The active issue reaches a stopping point without turning the recap into a grade or verdict. |

## Why the misread matters

The turn 5 misread is not automatically “useful because it caused thought.” It becomes analytically useful only because the researcher identifies the false substitution, explains the construct boundary, and the next question follows that correction. In another context, the same misread could waste time or pressure a novice into accepting an inappropriate outcome.

Use these questions when debriefing:

1. What knowledge allowed the researcher to reject the Oracle's premise?
2. Would a novice recognise that “confidence” and “critique quality” are different constructs?
3. What evidence of reasoning appears in turn 6?
4. What teaching friction could make that construct distinction visible before AI drafts the methods section?
5. What makes turn 9 a release rather than another layer of pressure?

## Day 2 co-research use

This supplied episode is an equal route for anyone who does not want to circulate a personal excerpt. Read it once deductively with C/R/X/M/★, then again inductively to propose a pattern not supplied by the code key. A second reader may correct or contest that pattern. Map any owner-approved additional area as extending, cross-cutting, or outside the supplied lenses—or record “none.” Write only a content-free joint memo and extension-map entry; no copy of another participant's material is needed or retained.

## Offline peer-Oracle version

If the live service is unavailable, one participant reveals only the Oracle turns, one at a time. The researcher answers before the next turn is revealed. A third person may observe and code the exchange. Reading the displayed turn aloud is an offline facilitation choice, not a feature of the live site.

The peer acting as Oracle should:

- ask the written question without embellishing it;
- follow the researcher's correction rather than defending the prompt;
- avoid rewriting the proposal or issuing a verdict;
- use the final question-free recap as the operational stopping point while preserving the researcher's right to stop earlier; and
- treat disagreement about a code as evidence to discuss, not a score to settle.

Continue in the [participant workbook](workbook.html#conduct-a-bounded-co-research-reading).
